Hi Alice / Clearshore team,

Thanks for sending — please find our consolidated responses below and the short evidence pack attached (redwood_residency_retention_answers.pdf). I've answered using the same numbering as your questionnaire; if you prefer a table export, I can produce a CSV.

1) Default data residency (hosted)- Default tenant data for hosted customers is stored in the cloud region selected at account creation. For U.S. customers the default is us-west-2 (Oregon) unless the customer requests a different region during onboarding. EU customers default to eu-west-1 (Ireland). Customers can request region locking as part of a contract (Dedicated/Private options available).

2) Retention windows (hosted)- Request metadata (timestamps, routing, per-request cost metrics): retained for 90 days by default for troubleshooting/billing.
- Request payloads (raw prompts): 30 days by default; customers can opt into shorter windows via account settings or a contract addendum.
- Model outputs (generated tokens): 30 days by default; separate opt-out available.
- Audit logs (admin events, access logs): retained for 365 days by default for security/audit purposes.

3) Deletion / erasure workflow- Standard erasure process: customer ticket -> verify account ownership -> schedule deletion job -> run deletion across primary stores + cached KV layers -> verify manifests written to S3 (sha256) -> close ticket. For hosted accounts this pipeline completes within 72 hours of verification for typical accounts; evidence manifests are retained for 180 days. The attached evidence pack includes an example manifest and a sanitized runbook excerpt showing CLI steps and verification checks.

4) Caching and backups- Inference-level KV/prefix caches are in-memory by default and not persisted beyond process lifetimes for hosted customers. Some model variants (compatibility fallbacks) may persist small caches to ephemeral SSD on the serving host; these are wiped on instance termination and are excluded from backups.
- Backups: persistent backups (DB snapshots) that include metadata and billing records are encrypted and retained as per our backup retention policy (90 days snapshot retention). Customer payloads are not included in long-term cross-region backups for hosted plans unless explicitly enabled.

5) Evidence artifacts and attestations- We can provide:
- S3 manifest example showing deleted object keys and verification hashes (included in PDF)
- Timestamped runbook excerpt for deletion job (included)
- High-level diagram of data flow showing residency boundaries

6) Exceptions and support for compliance requests- For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) where customers can require specific region pinning, HSM/KMS controls, and longer audit retention. We can include contract language for region lock and extended retention/erasure SLAs.

Attachments: redwood_residency_retention_answers.pdf (contains manifest sample + redact-friendly runbook excerpt + data flow diagram).

If you'd like, I can schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk through the evidence pack. Otherwise, flag any questions inline and we'll update the doc.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Solutions | Redwood Inference

Hi Tom — short answers to your two points:
- 72 hours is our operational target for hosted accounts (cases where verification is straightforward). It is not part of our standard TOS for the self-serve hosted tier; for contractual commitments (e.g., procurement/enterprise customers) we can include a binding SLA for deletion timelines as part of a Dedicated or enterprise-hosted agreement.
- The 180-day retention for deletion manifests is configurable for enterprise customers; for hosted customers we retain manifests for 180 days by default to support audit trail requests. We can extend or shorten that window by contract and can supply manifest exports on request.

If you want formal contract language for both items I can draft suggested clauses and loop legal.

Olga
Security & Compliance Solutions | Redwood Inference
